title: Cross-pool internship → junior conversion pathway (90-day pilot)
content:
Purpose:
This doc lays out a time-boxed pilot to convert high-performing interns from cross-functional internship pools into entry-level (junior) ICs. Objective is to test a structured 90-day conversion pathway that reduces time-to-productivity and increases retention for early-career hires. This is intentionally narrower than full hiring playbooks: focus = conversion mechanics, evaluation rubric, targeted onboarding, mentorship, and measurable signals.

Scope and constraints:
- Pilot cohort size: 6 interns across Eng (serving-runtime), Product (console-and-rollouts), and Solutions.
- Conversion target: offer 4 of 6 to junior IC roles at cohort end.
- Commitment: People Ops + Host managers + 2 mentor pairs per intern.
- Budget cap: equivalent of 0.5 FTE hiring budget for conversion-related activities (interviews, training stipends, buddy time).
- Not covered: external recruiting process for off-cycle hires, equity/compensation negotiations beyond standard levels.

Success metrics (primary):
1) Acceptance rate among interns offered a role >= 80%
2) New-hire 90-day productivity score (manager-rated) >= 3.5/5 for converted cohort
3) Retention at 12 months >= 85% (tracked post-pilot)
4) Time-to-first-meaningful-PR/feature <= 28 days

Secondary signals:
- Candidate net promoter (intern feedback) >= 4/5
- Hiring cost-per-conversion <= 60% of a standard external hire

Conversion timeline (high-level):
- Week 0: Pilot kickoff, selection of cohort (finalize by manager signoffs)
- Weeks 1–4: Focused project sprint + documented deliverables + weekly mentor checkpoints
- Week 5: Midpoint evaluation (rubric checkpoint) and dev plan adjustments
- Weeks 6–10: Ownership phase (intern leads a small scope) + rehearsal interview prep
- Week 11: Final interview loop (internal conversion panel)
- Week 12: Offers and onboarding schedule for converted hires

Selection and eligibility rules:
- Minimum of 10 weeks in an active internship at Redwood Inference OR cross-pool assignment of at least 6 weeks with positive feedback.
- Manager nomination required with short case for conversion readiness (200–400 words).
- Intern self-nomination allowed (requires manager concurrence).
- Not eligible if active performance improvement plan exists.

Evaluation rubric (used at weeks 5 and 11):
- Technical proficiency (0–5): code quality, debugging, system understanding, relevant infra awareness.
- Product sense & impact (0–5): shipping judgement, scope identification, user empathy for internal customers.
- Collaboration & communication (0–5): cross-team communication, stakeholder syncs, asynchronous writeups.
- Autonomy & learning velocity (0–5): ability to unblock, pick up new tech, incorporate feedback.
- Role-fit & motivation (0–5): desire for role, career alignment, culture add.
Scoring guidance: >= 18 total qualifies for conversion interview loop; 15–17 = conditional (requires follow-up task); <15 = suggest additional internship extension or external hire pipeline.

Conversion interview loop (Week 11) — structure and owners:
1) Technical pair (30 min) — hosted by host-team engineer; focus: small systems design + reading existing code and identifying improvements.
2) Code review exercise (take-home, 2–4 hours) — clear rubric for maintainability and testing.
3) Behavioral panel (30 min) — manager + mentor; focus on collaboration scenarios and feedback examples.
4) Role-specific mini-scope presentation (15 min) — intern presents the week-6 ownership work and plans for next 90 days if hired.
Scoring: each interviewer rates 0–5 and writes a 1–2 sentence note. Hiring committee aggregates.

Onboarding & ramp for converted hires (first 90 days checklist):
Day 0–7:
- Offer acceptance confirmation and payroll setup completed by People Ops (owner: Maya).
- Assign onboarding buddy (not direct manager) and mentor (technical).
- Schedule "First 2 weeks" roadmap with clear deliverables and 1:1 cadence.
- Accesses: code repos, infra read-only, ticketing, calendar sharing — checklist owner: IT onboarding.

Week 2–4:
- Small landing project assigned with clear acceptance criteria (owner: manager).
- Weekly manager 1:1 + mentor syncs (30 min each).
- Intro to company-specific inference stack training: short micro-lectures (2×30min) + lab exercises.

Month 1–3:
- Ownership of a small feature or reliability task with end-to-end responsibility.
- Biweekly demo to team for public feedback.
- Midpoint performance touchpoint at day 45 with documented goals and fast-feedback loop.
- End of 90-day evaluation using the same rubric with emphasis on progress and learning velocity.

Mentorship pairing and expectations:
- Buddy: peer-level, shadow pair programming once per week, async Slack support.
- Mentor: senior engineer, 1:1 weekly for 45 minutes, coach on system design and career navigation.
- Mentor checklist: initial 30-day plan, technical reading list, three concrete learning goals, remediation steps.
- Mentor compensation: 4 hours/week of allocated time recognized in manager bandwidth planning.

Documentation and artifacts required from intern during pilot:
- Weekly one-page update: accomplishments, blockers, next-week plan (post in shared drive folder).
- End-of-sprint writeup: summary of impact, lessons learned, suggested follow-ups.
- Final presentation deck (5–7 slides) for conversion panel.

Manager responsibilities (host managers):
- Nominate candidates and provide short conversion memo.
- Schedule time for pair sessions and code reviews.
- Provide weekly feedback and complete midpoint and final rubric.
- Reserve hiring budget slot and headcount trigger before Week 10.

People Ops responsibilities:
- Coordinate offers, comp bands, and conversion process logistics.
- Run final panel and compile decision notes.
- Provide standardized offer template and conversion-friendly L1 salary guidance.

Known risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Interns receive competing offers at conversion time. Mitigation: early-market check-ins; fast decision window (72 hours) for offers.
- Risk: Manager bandwidth to mentor/assess. Mitigation: cap mentors to 2 interns concurrently; manager signoff required prior to nomination.
- Risk: Skill mismatch for production readiness. Mitigation: conditional offers with 30-day probation and clear success criteria.

Open questions (to resolve in pilot design):
- Compensation level: use standard junior bands or custom ramped comp? (Action: finalize with Finance by Nov 14)
- Headcount vs conversion: do conversions need HR headcount approvals early? (Action: legal/finance check)
- Should converted hires have immediate access to production infra? propose staged access.

Next steps (owners and dates):
- Finalize cohort selection criteria and nomination form (Maya) — due 2025-11-12
- Confirm mentor pool and manager time commitments (Jonah) — due 2025-11-14
- Create panel rubric doc + interview schedule template (Priya) — due 2025-11-16
- Publish pilot comms to internal hiring channels and Slack (Evelyn) — planned 2025-11-18

Appendix (templates):
- Nomination snippet (200–400 words): "Candidate X consistently delivered Y, demonstrated Z, recommended for conversion because..."
- Weekly update template: 3 bullets: What I shipped; 1 blocker; next week plan.
- Midpoint rubric sheet: simple line-items for each axis with 0–5 scoring and required clarifying note for scores <=2.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally operational and experiment-oriented. I expect some items will change after first cohort — please leave comments in the doc and link any feedback to JIRA HR-3421.

Quick links: Confluence pilot page (CONF-7892) | JIRA HR-3421 | Slack channel #internship-pilot

-- Maya (People Ops)
